axisReviews.evidence: Individual freedom and opposition to censorship coexist with conventional security and weapons regulation.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Deregulation of commerce does not automatically imply decriminalising drugs or ending all policing.

axisReviews.evidence: Her equalities rhetoric favours individual treatment and shared civic identity over group-based politics.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Opposition to identity politics does not imply denial of minority citizenship or a general ban on cultural expression.

axisReviews.evidence: Growth-oriented visa reform and skilled recruitment coexist with control of irregular entry.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The brief premiership did not implement an unlimited settlement system; neutral caps/cultural-priority responses reflect balancing growth with controlled entry.

axisReviews.evidence: Her foreign-secretary record and UN speech favour deterrence and military aid to Ukraine.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Support for an attacked ally does not demonstrate endorsement of unrestricted autonomous killing or conscription.

axisReviews.evidence: Brexit sovereignty coexists with NATO, international cooperation and trade liberalisation.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: She changed from Remain to supporting Brexit; this period assesses the later stance without treating alliance limits as identical to EU integration.

axisReviews.evidence: Her growth programme favours private enterprise and investment rather than expanding state commercial ownership.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The NHS and temporary energy support remained central commitments; expenditure alone is not ownership.

axisReviews.evidence: International trade leadership and free-trade agreements favour tariff reduction and foreign investment.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Strategic dependence on Russia and China raised security exceptions; those do not establish broad agricultural protection.

axisReviews.evidence: Supply-side reform and investment zones prioritise market decisions and reduced regulation.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The Energy Price Guarantee was a large state intervention during a crisis; minimum wage and public money were retained.

axisReviews.evidence: The Growth Plan sought lower personal and business taxes rather than greater cash redistribution.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Energy support and proposed public services remained; tax cuts do not mean eliminating all benefits.

axisReviews.evidence: Government programmes rely on civil authority rather than clerical approval.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: The established church and ceremonial religion remained; no plan to eliminate every symbolic religious accommodation was found.

axisReviews.evidence: Support for same-sex marriage accompanies opposition to gender self-identification and some traditional institutional preferences.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Economic liberalism is not a proxy for every social issue; her mixed social record requires separate answers.

axisReviews.evidence: Planning reform, construction, energy supply and productivity are prioritised in the growth programme.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Long-term biomedical safety was not addressed; support for building does not warrant permissive embryo enhancement.

axisReviews.evidence: Investment zones and local growth mechanisms coexist with a national economic plan and unionist government.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Local incentives are not regional secession or complete fiscal independence; UK institutional analogies are qualified.

axisReviews.evidence: Her equalities programme emphasises opportunity and rejecting low expectations while treating sex as biological in specific contexts.
axisReviews.counterEvidence: Sex recognition does not prove general genetic determinism; no national IQ or racial aggression theory was found.
